title: Wait, Where's the iPhone 18? Apple Skipped It This Fall
summary:
Imagine waiting all year for your favorite candy bar. Then the company says, 'Surprise! We're only selling the giant deluxe version this time.' That's kind of what Apple just did with the iPhone.

Yesterday, Apple held its big yearly event to show off new phones. The star was the iPhone Duo — Apple's first foldable phone, shaped like a passport. There were also the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max, plus new AirPods and Apple Watches.

But wait. Where's the regular iPhone 18? The one that's not 'Pro'? The one that doesn't cost a fortune?

It's not here. Apple didn't announce it. This is the first time since 2019 that Apple hasn't launched the standard and Pro iPhones together. That's a big change.

Why would Apple do this? Maybe because the company now makes six different iPhones. Showing them all at once would be a lot. Also, the Pro models cost $100 more than last year — $1,199 and $1,299. Apple might be saving the cheaper phones for later.

Reports say Apple will probably announce the iPhone 18 next spring, along with maybe an iPhone Air 2 or a budget-friendly iPhone 18e. The standard iPhone is still the most popular model, so Apple won't leave fans waiting forever.

The iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max go on pre-order September 12 and hit stores September 18. The iPhone Duo pre-order starts October 16, with a launch on October 23.

So if you want a new iPhone this fall, you'll have to go big — or wait.
why_it_matters: It shows that things we really want don't always arrive on time, and that companies make big choices about money — worth talking about with your family before buying something new.

background_read: Apple is the company that makes the iPhone, and for years it has held a big September event to show off new phones before the holiday shopping season.
A 'foldable' phone has a screen that bends in half like a book — other phone companies such as Samsung have been selling them for several years.
The word 'Pro' on an iPhone means a fancier version with better cameras and features, and it costs more than the regular model.

WHAT: Apple skipped the regular iPhone 18 for the first time since 2019 and raised the Pro prices by $100.
WHERE: It all happened at Apple's big yearly event, with pre-orders starting September 12 and phones in stores September 18.
WHY: Apple now makes six different iPhones, and it may be saving the cheaper models — like a possible iPhone 18 or 18e — for next spring.

perspectives.description: They are thrilled about Apple's first foldable, the iPhone Duo shaped like a passport, and the newest Pro cameras.
Families may feel let down: the cheaper regular iPhone 18 isn't here yet, and the Pro models cost $100 more than last year.
They think splitting the launch into a fall event and a spring event could help Apple sell phones over a longer stretch of the year.
